product: Alexa+ Add-on developer tools (MCP Toolkit / Web Simulator)
task: Test a self-hosted MCP server inside a real Alexa+ conversation
steps_taken: Read the Alexa+ add-on setup guides, then the hackathon FAQ
expected_result: A way for hackathon entrants to load a self-hosted MCP server into the Alexa+ Web Simulator or a developer account
actual_result: The add-on tools (Category SDK, MCP Toolkit, CLI, Web Simulator) are preview-only for select partners; individual setup-guide pages do not say so, only the docs home page and the hackathon FAQ do
workaround: Built my own web simulator that acts as a real MCP client over Streamable HTTP (the path the FAQ allows)
actionable_suggestion: Put the preview/partner-only notice on every setup-guide page, and offer a sandboxed simulator for hackathon entrants so the end-user experience can be validated on the real surface

task: Install strands-agents next to the current MCP Python SDK in one environment
steps_taken: Checked PyPI metadata for strands-agents 1.59.0 and mcp before choosing versions
expected_result: strands-agents to accept the current MCP SDK release (mcp 2.3.0)
actual_result: strands-agents 1.59.0 declares mcp<2.2 so the newest MCP SDK cannot be used in the same environment
workaround: Pinned mcp>=2.1.1 and <2.2 for both the MCP server and the agent
actionable_suggestion: Publish a compatibility table for strands-agents vs mcp versions and widen the pin when a new MCP SDK minor ships

task: Plan Bedrock usage for the agent orchestrator
steps_taken: Read the official rules page before requesting credits
actual_result: Rules page states credit codes ran out on Oct 7, so Bedrock calls would be billed to the entrant
workaround: Kept the model provider pluggable and ran the Strands agent on Gemini's free tier through Strands' GeminiModel; Bedrock is not used
actionable_suggestion: Show remaining credit availability on the hackathon page or reserve a pool for late registrants so teams can plan AWS usage up front

task: Connect the Strands agent to a self-hosted MCP server that targets spec 2025-11-25
steps_taken: Created MCPClient with a streamable_http_client transport, recorded every HTTP request, listed tools and called one
expected_result: A way to choose the protocol version or force the initialize handshake, like mode='legacy' on the MCP SDK's own Client
actual_result: With mcp 2.x installed, MCPClient always probes server/discover at 2026-07-28 first and uses that era if the server accepts it; the constructor has no option to pin 2025-11-25
workaround: The server answers 2026-07-28 requests with -32022 naming 2025-11-25 as supported, so the client falls back to initialize and negotiates 2025-11-25
actionable_suggestion: Expose the SDK connect mode (or a protocol_version argument) on MCPClient and MCPServerConfig

task: Report a clear error when the MCP server is down
steps_taken: Started MCPClient against a closed localhost port inside an async request handler
expected_result: start() raises and leaves nothing behind
actual_result: start() raises MCPClientInitializationError as expected, but a RuntimeWarning follows: coroutine 'MCPClient.stop.<locals>._set_close_event' was never awaited
workaround: None needed for behaviour; the warning is noise in test output
actionable_suggestion: Await or cancel the close-event coroutine on the failed-start path

task: Keep an agent turn alive when the Gemini API is briefly overloaded
steps_taken: Ran the scenario evaluation against gemini-3.8-flash on the free tier with the default ModelRetryStrategy
expected_result: A 503 UNAVAILABLE ("model is currently experiencing high demand") to be retried with backoff like a 429
actual_result: GeminiModel only converts google-genai ClientError (429, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, UNAVAILABLE status on 4xx) to ModelThrottledException; a 503 arrives as ServerError and ends the turn on the first attempt
workaround: Subclassed GeminiModel to re-raise ServerError 500/503 as ModelThrottledException so the retry strategy backs off and retries
actionable_suggestion: Treat ServerError 503 (and 500) as throttling in GeminiModel.stream so the default retry strategy covers overload
evidence: src/hdr/orchestrator/llm.py; tests/unit/test_llm.py; evals/results/*probe-s01-LOW (fallback reason recorded per turn)

task: Hand a turn to the fallback agent quickly once the Gemini free-tier daily quota is used up
steps_taken: Ran three evaluation scenarios against gemini-3.8-flash after its free-tier daily quota (20 requests) had run out, with ModelRetryStrategy(max_attempts=4)
expected_result: The per-day quota error ends the model call at once (it cannot succeed before the daily reset) so the fallback answers in a few seconds
actual_result: GeminiModel raises ModelThrottledException for every 429, so the retry strategy backed off and retried the per-day quota error as well; each of the seven turns took 136 to 146 seconds before it failed and the rule agent answered
workaround: Moved to a model with a larger daily quota (gemini-3.5-flash-lite), kept the per-turn fallback to the rule agent, and made per-day quota errors non-retryable in a GeminiModel subclass so the fallback answers at once
actionable_suggestion: Tell per-day quota errors apart from per-minute rate limits (the 429 body names the quota) and do not retry the per-day ones, or honour the server's retry delay
evidence: evals/results/20261010T111456Z-dev-LOW/strands.jsonl (fallback reason and time for each turn); src/hdr/orchestrator/llm.py; tests/unit/test_llm.py::test_per_day_quota_is_not_retried

task: Decide which MCP protocol version the server should speak
steps_taken: Read the Alexa+ requirement ("MCP spec version 2025-11-25 (or a later version, once confirmed)"), then checked what the MCP Python SDK 2.1.1 server negotiates
expected_result: A list of the MCP versions that count, or the version the Alexa+ add-on runtime negotiates
actual_result: Nothing says whether 2026-07-28 is confirmed. The SDK server answers the 2026-07-28 era (server/discover) as well as 2025-11-25, so an unpinned server can end up on a version the rules may not accept
workaround: Pinned the server to 2025-11-25: requests in the newer era get -32022 naming 2025-11-25, and tests assert the negotiated version
actionable_suggestion: State in the rules or FAQ which MCP versions are accepted and which version Alexa+ add-ons use today

product: Hackathon FAQ and discussion forum (Alexa+ hosting)
task: Find out whether the MCP server has to stay online during judging
steps_taken: Read the FAQ entries on hosting, then the organizer answers in forum topics 45411 and 45493
expected_result: One answer: either a locally runnable repo plus video is enough, or the server must stay online until judging ends
actual_result: The FAQ says hosting isn't required and the MCP server doesn't need to stay running after submission; organizer answers in the forum say it needs to be live and accessible until the end of the judging period
workaround: Added a single-port container build (MCP server + agent API + simulator) so the demo can stay online through judging; the local run path is unchanged
actionable_suggestion: Correct the FAQ entry (or the forum answers) so both say the same thing; entrants plan hosting costs around this

product: Alexa+ MCP toolkit docs and the MCP Apps extension
task: Link the plan card to an MCP Apps view so Alexa+ could render it in its webview
steps_taken: Read the MCP toolkit overview and client-lifecycle pages, then the MCP Apps spec (2026-01-26) and its spec.types.ts
expected_result: One place for _meta.ui.resourceUri, and a statement of whether Alexa+ negotiates the io.modelcontextprotocol/ui extension
actual_result: The MCP Apps spec puts _meta.ui.resourceUri on the tool definition (tools/list). The Alexa+ client-lifecycle page shows it in a tools/call result, next to invoking/invoked strings, and its sample initialize uses protocol 2025-03-26 with no extensions capability. The overview page says Alexa+ supports MCP Apps but does not say which MCP Apps version its webview speaks.
workaround: Set _meta.ui.resourceUri on both the tool definitions and each result, and keep text and structured content for hosts without MCP Apps. Tested only in my own host.
actionable_suggestion: Say on the client-lifecycle page which location Alexa+ reads, whether it declares the io.modelcontextprotocol/ui capability, and which MCP Apps protocol version (e.g. 2026-01-26) the webview implements; add a tools/list example.
